candidate_1.name: SchNet 3D Graph Neural Network
candidate_1.approach: A continuous-filter convolutional neural network that takes 3D atomic coordinates and atomic numbers as inputs, computes invariant interatomic distances, and uses multi-task learning to predict all 16 QM8 electronic spectra properties.

constraints: must predict all 16 QM8 target properties
must use the provided harness.qm8_data loader

evaluation_protocol.split: 80% train, 10% validation, 10% test split with a fixed random seed
evaluation_protocol.metric: Mean Absolute Error (MAE) averaged across all 16 QM8 target properties

diagnostic_plan: Compute per-property MAE breakdown to identify which quantum-chemical methods (e.g., CC2 vs PBE0) or property types (excitation energies vs oscillator strengths) yield higher errors. Analyze error distribution histograms across molecular sizes (heavy atom counts).
validation_checkpoint: Run a 1-epoch dry run on 500 molecules to verify tensor shapes, loss gradients, and multi-task output dimensions.
budget_split: 50% architecture setup and data pipeline, 50% hyperparameter tuning and training optimization.

candidate_2_strategy.condition: If SchNet shows high error on oscillator strengths or struggles to converge across all 16 disparate quantum chemical levels of theory.
candidate_2_strategy.hypothesis: Incorporate angular and torsional geometric features using an angle-aware message-passing GNN (like DimeNet) or separate task heads to isolate differing levels of theory.

sources.title: SchNet: A continuous-filter convolutional neural network for modeling quantum interactions
